facts.value: The beneficial effect of exercise on the cardiovascular system is well documented.
facts.programme_association: Exercise and Health Fitness Management - BSc

facts.value: There is a direct correlation between physical inactivity and cardiovascular disease, and physical inactivity is an independent risk factor for the development of coronary artery disease.
facts.programme_association: Exercise and Health Fitness Management - BSc

facts.value: Low levels of physical exercise increase the risk of cardiovascular diseases mortality.
facts.programme_association: Exercise and Health Fitness Management - BSc

facts.value: Children who participate in physical exercise experience greater loss of body fat and increased cardiovascular fitness.
facts.programme_association: Exercise and Health Fitness Management - BSc

facts.value: Studies have shown that academic stress in youth increases the risk of cardiovascular disease in later years; however, these risks can be greatly decreased with regular physical exercise.
facts.programme_association: Exercise and Health Fitness Management - BSc

facts.value: There is a dose-response relationship between the amount of exercise performed from approximately 700–2000 kcal of energy expenditure per week and all-cause mortality and cardiovascular disease mortality in middle-aged and elderly men.
facts.programme_association: Exercise and Health Fitness Management - BSc

facts.value: The greatest potential for reduced mortality is seen in sedentary individuals who become moderately active.
facts.programme_association: Exercise and Health Fitness Management - BSc

facts.value: Studies have shown that since heart disease is the leading cause of death in women, regular exercise in aging women leads to healthier cardiovascular profiles.
facts.programme_association: Exercise and Health Fitness Management - BSc

facts.value: The most beneficial effects of physical activity on cardiovascular disease mortality can be attained through moderate-intensity activity (40–60% of maximal oxygen uptake, depending on age).
facts.programme_association: Exercise and Health Fitness Management - BSc

facts.value: After a myocardial infarction, survivors who changed their lifestyle to include regular exercise had higher survival rates.
facts.programme_association: Exercise and Health Fitness Management - BSc

facts.value: Sedentary people are most at risk for mortality from cardiovascular and all other causes.
facts.programme_association: Exercise and Health Fitness Management - BSc

facts.value: Some have suggested that increases in physical exercise might decrease healthcare costs, increase the rate of job attendance, as well as increase the amount of effort women put into their jobs.
